questions.q: Choose the correct form of the verb *be*: My sister ____ a nurse at the city hospital.
questions.topic: be with a singular subject in the present simple (is)
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: With a singular subject such as my sister, the present form of be is (is), like he / she / it.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct past form of *be*: I ____ very tired after the long journey yesterday.
questions.topic: be with I in the past simple (was)
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: In the past simple I takes (was), exactly like he / she / it, and not (were).

questions.q: Complete the negative form: The library ____ open last Friday because it was a holiday.
questions.topic: negative of be in the past simple (wasn't / weren't)
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: In the past the negative of be is (wasn't) with a singular subject and (weren't) with a plural one.

questions.q: Choose the correct question form: ____ your brothers at home now?
questions.topic: question form of be in the present simple (inversion)
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: To make a question we put be before the subject, and a plural subject takes (Are).

questions.q: Complete with the present continuous: The students ____ (sing) a beautiful song in the school hall at the moment.
questions.topic: present continuous with a plural subject (are + verb-ing)
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The present continuous is am / is / are + verb-ing, and a plural subject takes (are singing).

questions.q: Choose the correct pair: I ____ at home now, but last year I ____ in another city.
questions.topic: am and was with the subject I: present against past
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The subject I takes (am) in the present but (was) in the past, like he / she / it.

questions.q: Make this sentence negative: *She is helping her mother in the kitchen.*
options: She isn't helping her mother in the kitchen.
She doesn't helping her mother in the kitchen.
She not is helping her mother in the kitchen.
She isn't help her mother in the kitchen.
questions.topic: negative of the present continuous (isn't + verb-ing)
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: We add not to the verb be and keep the -ing form: isn't helping.

questions.q: What is the difference between *He is a teacher* and *He is teaching*?
options: The first describes his job; the second his action now.
The first describes the past; the second the future.
The first is a question; the second is a negative.
The first means exactly the same as the second.
questions.topic: be as a state against the present continuous for an action now
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: Be alone tells us about a state or a job, while the present continuous tells us about an action happening now.

questions.q: Change into a question: *They are waiting for the bus at the school gate.*
options: Are they waiting for the bus at the school gate?
Do they are waiting for the bus at the school gate?
They are waiting for the bus at the school gate?
Are they wait for the bus at the school gate?
questions.topic: yes / no question in the present continuous
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The question moves (are) before the subject and keeps the -ing form of the verb.

questions.q: Change into the negative and then into a question: *He was in the library yesterday evening.*
options: He wasn't in the library yesterday evening. / Was he in the library yesterday evening?
He didn't was in the library yesterday evening. / Did he was in the library yesterday evening?
He not was in the library yesterday evening. / Was he in the library yesterday evening?
He wasn't in the library yesterday evening. / He was in the library yesterday evening?
questions.topic: negative and question forms of be in the past simple
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The negative adds not to was (wasn't) with no helper verb, and the question puts was before the subject.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *It ____ raining heavily all day yesterday.*
questions.topic: was / were with singular subjects in the past continuous
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: In the past continuous, I / he / she / it take 'was': was + verb-ing.

questions.q: When do we use the past continuous tense?
options: For an action that was continuing at a certain time in the past
For an action that happens again and again every day
For an action that will happen at a certain time in the future
For an action that has just been finished a moment ago
questions.topic: the use of the past continuous (an action continuing at a past time)
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The past continuous shows an action that was continuing at a certain time in the past, as in: at 8 o'clock yesterday.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *My father ____ washing his car in the garden now.*
questions.topic: is with a singular subject in the present continuous
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: A singular subject (my father) takes 'is + verb-ing' in the present continuous with 'now'.

questions.q: Complete with the correct form: *The old man is ____ on the bed.* (lie)
questions.topic: verbs ending in -ie change to y before -ing (lie → lying)
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: A verb ending in -ie changes to -y before -ing: lie → lying.

questions.q: Choose the correct answer: *I ____ my homework when my mobile phone rang.*
questions.topic: the short past simple action interrupting the long past continuous action
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The long action takes the past continuous (was doing) and the short interrupting action takes the past simple (rang).

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *The players was running on the field when the coach arrived.*
options: The players were running on the field when the coach arrived.
The players was running on the field when the coach arrives.
The players are running on the field when the coach arrived.
The players were ran on the field when the coach arrived.
questions.topic: plural subjects take were in the past continuous
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: A plural subject (the players) takes 'were', not 'was', in the past continuous.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *My grandmother ____ all day yesterday, so she didn't cook.*
questions.topic: time expressions of the past continuous (all day yesterday)
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: 'All day yesterday' is a past continuous time expression, and a singular subject takes 'was'.

questions.q: In *Listen! The baby is crying.*, what does the word *Listen!* at the beginning show?
options: The action is happening now, at the moment of speaking
The action was happening at a time in the past
The action happens again and again every day
The action will happen at a time in the future
questions.topic: attention words (Look! / Listen!) with the present continuous
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: Words like 'Listen!' and 'Look!' draw attention to an action happening at the moment of speaking, so the present continuous is used.

questions.q: Make a question for the underlined word: *Nadia was writing __a letter__ in her room last night.*
options: What was Nadia writing in her room last night?
What Nadia was writing in her room last night?
What did Nadia writing in her room last night?
What were Nadia writing in her room last night?
questions.topic: making a question in the past continuous (helping verb before the subject)
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: In a past continuous question the helping verb comes before the subject: What was Nadia writing…?

questions.q: Change the sentence into the past continuous with the time 'at 8 o'clock yesterday': *My brothers are playing football in the club.*
options: My brothers were playing football in the club at 8 o'clock yesterday.
My brothers was playing football in the club at 8 o'clock yesterday.
My brothers are playing football in the club at 8 o'clock yesterday.
My brothers were play football in the club at 8 o'clock yesterday.
questions.topic: changing the present continuous into the past continuous
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - فعل الكينونة (am / is / are - was / were) والمضارع المستمر والماضي المستمر
questions.why: The present continuous (are playing) becomes the past continuous (were playing) with a past time expression.

Language review 1 › Talking about two ev.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي

questions.q: When we talk about two events in the past and want to show which one happened first, which tense do we use for the earlier event?
questions.topic: Tense of the earlier event
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: The event that happened first takes the past perfect (had + past participle); the later event takes the past simple.

questions.q: Complete with the correct form: *When I got to the party, everyone ____ home.* (go)
questions.topic: Form of the past perfect: had + past participle
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: The past perfect is had + past participle, and the participle of 'go' is 'gone', so 'had gone' is correct.

questions.q: Which sentence uses the negative past perfect correctly?
options: She hadn't seen the message before she left the office.
She didn't had seen the message before she left the office.
She hadn't saw the message before she left the office.
She hasn't seen the message before she left the office.
questions.topic: Negative past perfect: hadn't + past participle
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: The negative past perfect is hadn't + past participle, so 'hadn't seen' is right and 'hadn't saw' is wrong.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *The plane had taken off before we ____ the airport.* (reach)
questions.topic: Past simple after 'before'
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: The lesson states that the verb after 'before' is in the past simple, while the earlier event keeps the past perfect.

questions.q: Look at the two events: *Rana missed the bus. She woke up late.* Which sentence shows correctly that waking up late happened first?
options: Rana missed the bus because she had woken up late.
Rana had missed the bus because she woke up late.
Rana missed the bus because she has woken up late.
Rana missed the bus because she had wake up late.
questions.topic: 'because' + past perfect for the reason
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: The reason happened first, and the lesson says the reason after 'because' takes the past perfect: 'had woken up'.

questions.q: What is the difference between the tense used after 'after' and the tense used after 'before' in this lesson?
options: After 'after' we use the past perfect, but after 'before' we use the past simple.
After 'after' we use the past simple, but after 'before' we use the past perfect.
After both 'after' and 'before' we use the past perfect.
After both 'after' and 'before' we use the past simple.
questions.topic: 'after' vs 'before' + tense
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: The rule is: the verb after 'after' is past perfect, while the verb after 'before' is past simple.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *The match ____ by the time we reached the stadium.* (start)
questions.topic: 'by the time' + past perfect
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: With 'by the time' the earlier action takes the past perfect: 'had started'.

questions.q: *When we arrived at the hall, the ceremony had already begun.* Which event happened first?
options: The two events happened at the same time.
The ceremony had not begun when we arrived.
questions.topic: Identifying which event happened first
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: 'Had already begun' is the past perfect, so the ceremony began before we arrived.

questions.q: Join the two sentences in one sentence with 'after': *She finished her dinner. Then she went out with her friends.*
options: After she had finished her dinner, she went out with her friends.
After she finished her dinner, she had gone out with her friends.
After she has finished her dinner, she went out with her friends.
After she had finished her dinner, she had gone out with her friends.
questions.topic: Joining two sentences with 'after'
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: With 'after', the earlier action takes the past perfect and the later action takes the past simple.

questions.q: Rewrite the sentence using 'before' so that the meaning stays the same: *After he had locked the door, he left the office.*
options: He had locked the door before he left the office.
He locked the door before he had left the office.
He had locked the door before he had left the office.
He has locked the door before he left the office.
questions.topic: Rewriting with 'before'
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: The earlier action keeps the past perfect, and the verb after 'before' must be in the past simple.

questions.q: Complete the rule: the past perfect is formed with ____ + the past participle.
questions.topic: Form of the past perfect
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: The past perfect is always had + the third form of the verb: had worked, had eaten, had gone.

questions.q: Choose the correct past participle of each verb: *write / break / help*
questions.topic: Past participle of irregular verbs
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: The past perfect needs the third form of the verb: write - wrote - written, break - broke - broken, help - helped.

questions.q: Look at the sentence and choose why it is wrong: *After Nadia had washed the dishes, she had watched TV.*
options: 'had watched' is wrong: the second event takes the past simple 'watched'
'had washed' is wrong: it should be the past simple 'washed'
'after' must be followed by the present perfect form 'has watched'
Both verbs must be in the past perfect to show two past events
questions.topic: Using the past perfect for the first event only
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: Only the earlier event (washing the dishes) takes the past perfect; the later event stays in the past simple: she watched TV.

questions.q: What is the difference in meaning between these two sentences? *When we arrived, the film started.* / *When we arrived, the film had started.*
options: In the second sentence the film started first, then we arrived
In the first sentence the film started first, then we arrived
The two sentences mean exactly the same thing
In the second sentence the film started after we arrived
questions.topic: Difference between 'started' and 'had started' after 'when'
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: The past perfect 'had started' shows the film started before we arrived; 'started' puts the two events at about the same time.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *Huda was hungry because she hadn't ate her breakfast.*
options: *Huda was hungry because she hadn't eaten her breakfast.*
*Huda was hungry because she didn't ate her breakfast.*
*Huda was hungry because she hadn't eat her breakfast.*
*Huda was hungry because she hasn't eaten her breakfast.*
questions.topic: 'hadn't' + past participle (hadn't eaten, not hadn't ate)
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: After hadn't we use the past participle: eat - ate - eaten, so the correct form is hadn't eaten.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct form: *The children were excited because they ____ a lion before.* (never / see)
questions.topic: Past perfect with 'never' for an earlier experience
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: The earlier experience takes the past perfect, and after had we use the participle: had never seen.

questions.q: Rewrite the two sentences as one, using *By the time*: *I finished my homework. Then my father came home.*
options: *By the time my father came home, I had finished my homework.*
*By the time my father had come home, I finished my homework.*
*By the time my father came home, I have finished my homework.*
*By the time my father came home, I had finish my homework.*
questions.topic: Joining two past events with 'By the time'
questions.lesson: Talking about two events in the past | الحديث عن حدثين في الماضي
questions.why: By the time + past simple comes with the later event, and the earlier action takes the past perfect: had finished.

Language review 1 › Review of tenses - ا.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)

questions.q: Choose the correct form: *My father ____ to work by bus every day.* (go)
questions.topic: Third person singular -es with he / she / it
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: 'My father' is he, and with he / she / it we add -es to the verb: go → goes.

questions.q: Complete with the correct form of *have*: *Our new teacher ____ a white car.*
questions.topic: have becomes has with he / she / it
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: With he / she / it, have becomes has — the lesson states clearly it is not 'haves'.

questions.q: Choose the correct negative form: *Sami ____ watch TV every evening.*
questions.topic: Negative present simple with doesn't + base form
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: 'Sami' is he and the time is every evening, so the negative is doesn't + base form.

questions.q: Choose the correct question word: *____ Fatima study in the school library every day?*
questions.topic: Does + subject + base form in present simple questions
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: 'Fatima' is she, so the present simple question starts with Does + subject + base form.

questions.q: Which verb in the list is NOT a regular verb? *cooked / washed / bought / climbed*
questions.topic: Regular verbs (-ed) vs irregular verbs
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: Cooked, washed and climbed take -ed, but bought is an irregular past form that must be memorised.

questions.q: Why is this sentence wrong? *We visit our uncle last week.*
options: Because 'visit' is an irregular verb, so it cannot take -ed.
Because 'we' always takes the -s form of the verb in the past.
Because 'last week' is a finished past time, so we need the past simple 'visited'.
Because the present simple is used with all past time words.
questions.topic: Matching the tense to the time marker
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: 'Last week' is a finished past time, so the past simple 'visited' is required, not the present 'visit'.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *They didn't went to the museum.*
options: They didn't go to the museum.
They don't go to the museum.
They didn't gone to the museum.
They not went to the museum.
questions.topic: didn't + base form in the negative past
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: After didn't we use the base form: didn't go, not 'didn't went'.

questions.q: Choose the correct question word: *____ the students answer all the questions yesterday?*
questions.topic: Did + subject + base form in past simple questions
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: 'Yesterday' is a finished past time, so the question is Did + subject + base form.

questions.q: Make a question for the underlined words: *Ahmed met __his teacher__ at the airport this morning.*
options: Who Ahmed met at the airport this morning?
Who did Ahmed met at the airport this morning?
Who did Ahmed meet at the airport this morning?
Who does Ahmed meet at the airport this morning?
questions.topic: Making a past question for an underlined object
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: The underlined words are the object, so the question is Who + did + subject + base form (meet).

questions.q: Change this sentence into the negative: *Nadia finished her project yesterday.*
options: Nadia didn't finished her project yesterday.
Nadia doesn't finish her project yesterday.
Nadia not finished her project yesterday.
Nadia didn't finish her project yesterday.
questions.topic: Transforming a past simple sentence into the negative
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: The past negative is didn't + base form, so 'finished' goes back to 'finish'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct past simple form: *My sister ____ her bedroom yesterday morning.* (tidy)
questions.topic: Past simple spelling: consonant + y
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: A verb ending in a consonant + y changes the y to i and adds -ed: tidy → tidied.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the past simple of the verb in brackets: *He ____ his little brother to the park yesterday.* (take)
questions.topic: Irregular past form of 'take'
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: 'Take' is an irregular verb, so its past simple form is 'took', not 'taked'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the past simple of the verb in brackets: *The shop ____ at nine o'clock last night.* (close)
questions.topic: Past simple spelling: verbs ending in -e
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: A verb ending in -e adds only -d in the past simple: close → closed.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the past simple of the verb in brackets: *He ____ his phone on the wet floor.* (drop)
questions.topic: Past simple spelling: doubling the final consonant
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: A short verb ending in consonant + vowel + consonant doubles the last letter before -ed: drop → dropped.

questions.q: Choose the correct form to complete the sentence: *My uncle ____ in a small village for ten years, but now he lives in Cairo.*
questions.topic: Present simple vs past simple: finished actions
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: 'For ten years' and 'now he lives in Cairo' show a finished period in the past, so the past simple 'lived' is needed.

questions.q: What is the difference in meaning between these two sentences? *We watch the news every evening.* / *We watched the news yesterday evening.*
options: The first is a habit that is still true; the second is a finished action.
The first is a finished action; the second is a habit that is still true.
Both sentences describe a habit that is still true now.
Both sentences describe a finished action in the past.
questions.topic: Habit vs finished past action
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: The present simple describes a habit that is still true, while the past simple describes something that ended.

questions.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence: *My cousin don't like fish.*
questions.topic: doesn't with a singular subject
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: With a singular subject like 'my cousin' we use 'doesn't' + the base verb 'like'.

questions.q: Make a question for this past simple sentence: *Karim visited the dentist last week.*
options: Did Karim visit the dentist last week?
Did Karim visited the dentist last week?
Does Karim visit the dentist last week?
Karim did visit the dentist last week?
questions.topic: Did + base verb in past questions
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: Past simple questions are formed with Did + subject + base verb, so 'visit' stays in the base form.

questions.q: Make a question for the underlined words: *They moved to __Taiz__ last summer.*
options: Where did they move last summer?
Where did they moved last summer?
Where do they move last summer?
questions.topic: Wh-questions in the past simple
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: The underlined words answer 'Where', so the question is Where + did + subject + base verb.

questions.q: Rewrite this sentence in the past simple: *The students write a report about water and take photos of the valley.*
options: The students wrote a report about water and took photos of the valley.
The students writed a report about water and taked photos of the valley.
The students written a report about water and taken photos of the valley.
The students wrote a report about water and taked photos of the valley.
questions.topic: Two irregular verbs in one past sentence
questions.lesson: Review of tenses - المضارع البسيط والماضي البسيط (الأفعال المنتظمة وغير المنتظمة)
questions.why: Both verbs are irregular, so write → wrote and take → took in the past simple.

Language review 3 › Reporting what peopl.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *My uncle ____ us that he would visit us on Friday.*
questions.topic: told + object (said vs told)
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: Told must be followed by the person we spoke to (my uncle told us), while said cannot take a person directly.

questions.q: Complete the reported sentence: *'I work in a hospital,' Salma said.* → *Salma said that she ____ in a hospital.*
questions.topic: Present simple to past simple in reported speech
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: Because the reporting verb said is in the past, the present simple work moves one step back to the past simple worked.

questions.q: What is reported speech?
options: Telling someone what another person said, using your own words
Writing a person's exact words inside quotation marks
A report that a student writes about a school trip
A sentence that must always begin with the word that
questions.topic: Reported speech vs direct speech
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: In reported speech we tell another person what was said without repeating the exact words; direct speech keeps the exact words.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *Amina said ____ her sister that she would come back soon.*
questions.topic: said to + person
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: With said we put to before the person we are speaking to: said to her sister.

questions.q: Complete the reported sentence: *'We are preparing for the exam,' the students said.* → *The students said that they ____ for the exam.*
questions.topic: Present continuous to past continuous
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: The present continuous are preparing moves back to the past continuous were preparing, and we changes to they.

questions.q: Complete the reported sentence: *'I have finished my project,' Omar said.* → *Omar said that he ____ his project.*
questions.topic: Present perfect to past perfect
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: With a past reporting verb, the present perfect have finished moves back to the past perfect had finished.

questions.q: Choose the correct reported sentence: *'You should drink more water,' the nurse said.*
options: The nurse said that I should drink more water.
The nurse said that I shall drink more water.
The nurse said that I should drank more water.
The nurse said that I would drink more water.
questions.topic: Modals that do not change (should)
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: Could, would, should and might do not change in reported speech, so should stays should.

questions.q: Complete the reported sentence: *'You must wear a helmet,' the coach told the players.* → *The coach told the players that they ____ wear a helmet.*
questions.topic: must changes to had to
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: In this lesson must changes to had to when the reporting verb is in the past.

questions.q: Report this sentence: *'I will finish my homework before dinner,' Fahd said.*
options: Fahd said that he would finish his homework before dinner.
Fahd said that he will finish his homework before dinner.
Fahd said that I would finish my homework before dinner.
Fahd said that he would finished his homework before dinner.
questions.topic: will to would + pronoun and possessive change
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: Three changes together: I becomes he, will becomes would, and my becomes his.

questions.q: Report this sentence: *'We saw the thief in the market,' the boys told the police.*
options: The boys told the police that they had seen the thief in the market.
The boys told the police that they saw the thief in the market.
The boys told the police that we had seen the thief in the market.
The boys told to the police that they had seen the thief in the market.
questions.topic: Past simple to past perfect + pronoun change
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: Two changes together: we becomes they, and the past simple saw moves back to the past perfect had seen.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *'I can swim 100 metres,' Tariq explained.* Tariq explained that he ____ swim 100 metres.
questions.topic: can → could backshift
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: 'Can' becomes 'could' when the reporting verb is in the past.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *'I will bring the books,' Hassan promised.* Hassan promised that he ____ bring the books.
questions.topic: will → would backshift
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: 'Will' becomes 'would' after a past reporting verb such as 'promised'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *'I have made a big mistake,' the driver admitted.* The driver admitted that he ____ a big mistake.
questions.topic: present perfect → past perfect backshift
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: The present perfect 'have made' moves back to the past perfect 'had made'.

questions.q: Choose the correct reported sentence: *'I am busy,' Sami said to Layla.*
options: Sami told Layla that he was busy.
Sami said Layla that he was busy.
Sami told that he was busy.
Sami told Layla that he is busy.
questions.topic: said vs told with an object
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: 'Tell' needs a person after it, so we say 'told Layla', and the verb moves back to 'was'.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *My brother complained that he didn't liked the soup.*
options: My brother complained that he didn't like the soup.
My brother complained that he doesn't liked the soup.
My brother complained that he didn't likes the soup.
My brother complained that he not liked the soup.
questions.topic: base form after didn't
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: After 'didn't' the verb stays in the base form, so it is 'didn't like', not 'didn't liked'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *'I do my homework before dinner,' Nabil replied.* Nabil replied that he did ____ homework before dinner.
questions.topic: possessive pronoun change (my → his)
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: When Nabil reports his own words, 'my' changes to 'his' because the speaker is Nabil.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *'I am looking for a new job,' Maha mentioned.* Maha mentioned that she ____ for a new job.
questions.topic: present continuous → past continuous backshift
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: The present continuous 'am looking' moves back to the past continuous 'was looking'.

questions.q: Report this sentence: *'I can't drive, but I am learning,' Saeed insisted.*
options: Saeed insisted that he couldn't drive, but (that) he was learning.
Saeed insisted that he can't drive, but (that) he was learning.
Saeed insisted that he couldn't drive, but (that) he is learning.
Saeed insisted that he doesn't drive, but (that) he learned.
questions.topic: changing both parts of an and/but sentence
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: Both parts of the sentence change together: 'can't' → 'couldn't' and 'am learning' → 'was learning'.

questions.q: Report this sentence: *'I haven't seen my family for a month,' the soldier wrote.*
options: The soldier wrote that he hadn't seen his family for a month.
The soldier wrote that he hasn't seen his family for a month.
The soldier wrote that he didn't see his family for a month.
The soldier wrote that he hadn't saw his family for a month.
questions.topic: negative present perfect → past perfect
questions.lesson: Reporting what people say - تغيير الأزمنة عند نقل الكلام (said / told)
questions.why: 'Haven't seen' moves back to 'hadn't seen' with the past participle, and 'my' changes to 'his'.

Language review 2 › Expressing purpose w.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر

questions.q: What does 'to' + infinitive tell us in a sentence?
questions.topic: Meaning of purpose with 'to' + infinitive
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: 'to' + infinitive answers the question 'Why?', so it gives the purpose of the action.

questions.q: Complete: *They worked all summer ____ enough money for the trip.*
questions.topic: Bare infinitive after 'to'
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: After 'to' the verb is always the bare infinitive: to earn, never to earning or to earned.

questions.q: Complete: *We met last night ____ the new plan with the manager.*
questions.topic: Tense does not change the infinitive
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: The past time 'last night' does not change the form after 'to'; the infinitive stays 'to discuss'.

questions.q: Which sentence is correct?
options: Nadia went to the market for some fish.
Nadia went to the market for buy some fish.
Nadia went to the market for to buy some fish.
Nadia went to the market for buying some fish.
questions.topic: 'for' + noun, not 'for' + infinitive
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: 'for' is followed by a noun (some fish); purpose is expressed with 'to buy', not with 'for buy'.

questions.q: Choose the correct option: *He left the house quietly ____ wake the baby.*
questions.topic: Negative purpose with 'so as not to'
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: A negative purpose uses 'so as not to' + infinitive; the other forms give the opposite meaning.

questions.q: Rewrite using a more formal purpose phrase: *She trained every day because she wanted to win the race.*
options: She trained every day in order to win the race.
She trained every day in order not to win the race.
She trained every day in order to winning the race.
She trained every day for win the race.
questions.topic: Rewriting a reason clause with 'in order to'
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: 'in order to' + infinitive is the more formal equivalent of 'because she wanted to', with the same meaning.

questions.q: Answer the question with a purpose phrase: *Why did she take a taxi to the station?*
options: To get to the station on time.
For get to the station on time.
To getting to the station on time.
For getting to the station on time.
questions.topic: Answering 'Why?' with a purpose phrase
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: The purpose clause that answers 'Why?' is 'to' + infinitive: to get.

questions.q: Complete the instruction: *Hold the door open ____ the old man pass.*
questions.topic: Purpose after an imperative in instructions
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: Instructions are built as imperative + 'to' + infinitive, as in 'Hold the door open to let him pass'.

questions.q: Join the two sentences into one using 'so as to': *The team practised every evening. They wanted to improve their passing.*
options: The team practised every evening so as to improve their passing.
The team practised every evening so as improve their passing.
The team practised every evening so as to improving their passing.
The team practised every evening so as for improve their passing.
questions.topic: Joining two sentences with 'so as to'
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: 'so as to' must be followed by the bare infinitive, so the two sentences join as 'so as to improve'.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *He took a part-time job for pay his university fees.*
options: He took a part-time job to pay his university fees.
He took a part-time job to paying his university fees.
He took a part-time job for paid his university fees.
He took a part-time job for to pay his university fees.
questions.topic: Correcting 'for' + infinitive errors
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: 'for' cannot take an infinitive; purpose needs 'to' + infinitive, so 'for pay' becomes 'to pay'.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct negative purpose phrase: *He wrote the address down ____ forget it.*
questions.topic: Negative purpose: 'so as not to'
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: 'So as not to + infinitive' is the negative purpose form: he wrote the address down so that he would not forget it.

questions.q: Complete with the correct form of the verb: *She opened the window to ____ some fresh air.*
questions.topic: Verb form after 'to' of purpose
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: After 'to' of purpose we always use the base form of the verb, so 'get' is the correct form here.

questions.q: Choose the correct form: *We go to the shop every morning ____ fresh bread.*
questions.topic: Common error: 'for' + base verb after a verb of movement
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: Purpose is expressed by 'to + base verb', so 'to buy' is right and 'for buy' is the mistake the lesson warns about.

questions.q: Complete the sentence correctly: *Yesterday he went to the garage ____ his car.*
questions.topic: Infinitive after 'to' with a past main verb
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: The main verb 'went' is past, but after 'to' the verb stays in the base form: to repair.

questions.q: Which word completes the sentence: *Wear a heavy coat ____ keep warm in winter.*
questions.topic: Choosing 'to' as the purpose connector
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: 'To' before a base verb shows purpose; 'for', 'so' and 'because' cannot join a bare verb like 'keep' here.

questions.q: Which sentence has the same meaning as: *She spoke quietly so as not to wake the children.*
options: She spoke quietly because she did not want to wake the children.
She spoke quietly although the children were already awake.
She spoke quietly and then woke the children up.
She did not speak at all because the children were sleeping.
questions.topic: Meaning of 'so as not to'
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: 'So as not to wake' means she did not want to wake the children, so she spoke quietly.

questions.q: Join these two sentences using the purpose phrase 'to': *He wants to win the race. He trains every morning.*
options: He trains every morning to win the race.
He trains every morning to winning the race.
He trains every morning for win the race.
He trains every morning to won the race.
questions.topic: Joining two sentences with 'to' of purpose
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: The purpose phrase 'to + base verb' is joined to the second sentence: He trains every morning to win the race.

questions.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence: *They went to the station to meeting their uncle.*
options: They went to the station to meet their uncle.
They went to the station to met their uncle.
They went to the station for meet their uncle.
They went to the station for meeting their uncle.
questions.topic: Correcting a wrong verb form after 'to'
questions.lesson: Expressing purpose with 'to' + infinitive | التعبير عن الغرض بـ to + المصدر
questions.why: After 'to' of purpose the verb must be in the base form, so 'to meeting' is corrected to 'to meet'.

Language review 4 › Comparison of adject.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *The internet is ____ than the post for sending messages.*
questions.topic: Comparative form with 'than'
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: One-syllable adjectives take -er before 'than': quicker than the post.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *The Burj Khalifa is ____ building in the world.*
questions.topic: 'the' before a superlative
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: 'The' is always used before a superlative: the tallest building in the world.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *Huda is the youngest ____ the four sisters.*
questions.topic: 'of' + group after a superlative
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: 'Of' is used before a number or a group: the youngest of the four sisters.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *My new phone is as ____ as my old one.*
questions.topic: 'as ... as' with the plain adjective
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: With 'as ... as' we use the plain adjective, not the comparative: as good as.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *A bicycle is slow; it is ____ a car.*
questions.topic: Negative comparison: 'not as ... as'
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: The negative form is 'not as + plain adjective + as': not as fast as a car.

questions.q: Choose the correct word order: *Mr. Ali is ____ than Mr. Saeed.*
questions.topic: Word order: a + more + adjective + noun
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: With 'more' the order is a + more + adjective + noun: a more patient teacher.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *That was the most exciting match I have ____ watched.*
questions.topic: 'ever' with the present perfect after a superlative
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: With the present perfect and a superlative we use 'ever': the best film I have ever seen.

questions.q: Complete the sentence: *The weather today is ____ than it was yesterday.*
questions.topic: Irregular comparative 'worse'
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: The irregular comparative of 'bad' is 'worse': worse than it was yesterday.

questions.q: Rewrite the sentence using the superlative: *Cairo is bigger than any other city in Egypt.*
options: Cairo is the biggest city in Egypt.
Cairo is biggest city in Egypt.
Cairo is the bigger city in Egypt.
Cairo is the most big city in Egypt.
questions.topic: Rewriting a comparative with 'any other' as a superlative
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: 'Bigger than any other city in Egypt' means it is the biggest city in Egypt.

questions.q: Rewrite the sentence using 'than': *The train is not as slow as the bus.*
options: The bus is more slow than the train.
The bus is slower than the train.
The bus is slowest than the train.
The bus is as slow as the train.
questions.topic: Rewriting 'not as ... as' with 'than'
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: 'The train is not as slow as the bus' means the bus is slower than the train.

questions.q: Complete the rule from the lesson: *If you see ____ after the adjective, use the comparative form; if you see ____ before the gap, use the superlative form.*
questions.topic: than vs the: choosing comparative or superlative
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: The key rule of the lesson: 'than' after the adjective means comparative, and 'the' before it means superlative.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the adjective in brackets: *The museum is ____ from the station than the hotel is.* (far)
questions.topic: comparative of the irregular adjective far
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: 'Far' is irregular (far – farther/further) and 'than' shows a comparison, so 'farther' is correct.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the adjective in brackets: *This is ____ story I have ever read.* (good)
questions.topic: superlative of the irregular adjective good with the
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: 'Good' is irregular (good – better – best), and a superlative must take 'the' before it.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the adjective in brackets: *This dictionary is ____ than the old one.* (useful)
questions.topic: two-syllable adjectives not ending in -y take more
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: 'Useful' has two syllables and does not end in -y, so it takes 'more', not '-er'.

questions.q: Why does the sentence use *the most* and not *more*? *The Grand Mosque in Sana'a is the most beautiful building in the old city.*
options: Because 'beautiful' is a short adjective of one syllable.
Because 'the' and 'in the old city' show a superlative.
Because the adjective is followed by the word 'than'.
questions.topic: why the most is used with the and a defining phrase
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: 'The' before the adjective and 'in the old city' after it show a superlative, so the adjective takes 'the most'.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *This medicine works better then the other one.*
options: This medicine works gooder than the other one.
This medicine works more better than the other one.
This medicine works better than the other one.
This medicine works as better as the other one.
questions.topic: than vs then spelling
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: 'Then' means 'after that'; comparison needs 'than', so 'better than' is the correct form.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the adjective in brackets: *This room is not as ____ as the one upstairs.* (big)
questions.topic: as … as takes the plain adjective
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: 'As … as' takes the plain adjective, never the comparative; 'as bigger as' is wrong.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct form of the adjective in brackets: *She has never stayed in ____ hotel than this one.* (comfortable)
questions.topic: a + more + adjective in a comparison with than
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: 'Than' shows a comparison, and 'a' before the gap rules out 'the most'.

questions.q: Rewrite the two sentences as one sentence, using a comparative adjective and 'than': *The blue car is fast. The red car is very fast.*
options: The red car is the fastest than the blue car.
The blue car is faster than the red car.
The red car is faster than the blue car.
The red car is more fast than the blue car.
questions.topic: combining two sentences into one comparative sentence
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: The two sentences are joined with comparative + 'than': the red car is faster than the blue car.

questions.q: Rewrite the sentence with the same meaning, using the word in brackets: *No student in the class is as clever as Salem.* (clever)
options: Salem is cleverer than the class.
Salem is the cleverer student in the class.
Salem is as clever as the class.
Salem is the cleverest student in the class.
questions.topic: rewriting an as … as sentence as a superlative
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - استخدام المقارنة والتفضيل في الجملة (than / the)
questions.why: 'No student is as clever as Salem' means Salem is the cleverest of all, so 'the cleverest' is used.

Language review 3 › Tense review: Talkin.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)

questions.q: Choose the correct answer: *I think our school team ____ win the cup next Friday.*
questions.topic: Form of 'will' + infinitive for predictions
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: 'will' never changes with the subject and is always followed by the infinitive without 'to' when we predict the future.

questions.q: The present continuous (am / is / are + -ing) with a future time expression is used for…
options: arrangements that have already been agreed with other people
predictions about the future and quick decisions made while speaking
promises that people make at the moment of speaking
habits and actions that are repeated every week or every month
questions.topic: Use of the present continuous for future arrangements
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: This form describes something already arranged with other people, as in 'We are moving to a new flat on Friday.'

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct future form: *We ____ visit our grandparents in Ibb next month; we have already decided.*
questions.topic: 'am / is / are + going to' for intentions and plans
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: 'going to' + infinitive expresses a decision already made, and with 'we' the correct form is 'are going to'.

questions.q: Choose the correct answer: *The sky is clear, so it ____ rain tonight.*
questions.topic: Negative form 'won't' (will not)
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: The negative of 'will' is 'won't' (will not), as in 'It won't snow tonight.'

questions.q: Look at the sentence: *Look at that dog! It is going to jump into the river.* Why does the speaker use 'going to'?
options: Because the prediction is based on something we can see happening now
Because the action was arranged with another person before we spoke
Because the speaker is making a promise at the moment of speaking
Because the action is repeated every day at the same time
questions.topic: Predictions based on present evidence ('going to')
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: 'going to' also expresses a prediction supported by evidence we can see at the moment of speaking.

questions.q: To show that the present continuous means the future, which time expression completes: *He is playing football ____*?
questions.topic: The future time expression needed with the present continuous
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: Without a future time expression the present continuous means 'now', so a word like 'tomorrow afternoon' is necessary.

questions.q: Which sentence describes a decision made at the moment of speaking, not a plan arranged before?
options: I'm going to visit my aunt in Taiz this weekend.
We're playing a match on Saturday morning.
I'm going to start a new job in September.
questions.topic: 'will' for decisions made at the moment of speaking
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: 'will' is used for a quick decision taken while speaking, while the other three sentences are plans or arrangements.

questions.q: What does the speaker mean by the underlined words? *I __am seeing__ the dentist at ten tomorrow morning.*
options: The appointment has already been arranged
The speaker is at the dentist's now
The speaker is promising to visit the dentist
The speaker goes to the dentist every morning
questions.topic: Meaning of the present continuous in a fixed future arrangement
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: 'am seeing' with 'at ten tomorrow morning' shows a fixed arrangement, not an action happening now.

questions.q: Make a question for the underlined words: *They are flying to Socotra __next Monday__.*
options: When are they flying to Socotra?
When they are flying to Socotra?
When do they flying to Socotra?
When are they fly to Socotra?
questions.topic: Question form with the present continuous about a future arrangement
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: In the question 'are' comes before the subject and the verb keeps the -ing form: 'When are they flying…?'

questions.q: Make a question with 'going to' from the sentence: *You are going to study engineering at university.*
options: Are you going to study engineering at university?
Do you going to study engineering at university?
You are going to study engineering at university?
Are you going study engineering at university?
questions.topic: Question form 'Are you going to …?'
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: With 'going to' we put 'are' before the subject and keep 'going to' + infinitive: 'Are you going to study…?'

questions.q: Which order shows the three future forms from the weakest to the strongest in certainty?
options: will → going to → the present continuous
going to → will → the present continuous
the present continuous → going to → will
will → the present continuous → going to
questions.topic: order of certainty: will, going to, present continuous
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: The lesson orders them from the weakest to the strongest: will, then going to, then the present continuous.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct word: *My sister ____ going to learn French next year.*
questions.topic: am/is/are before going to
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: going to must be preceded by am/is/are, and the singular subject My sister takes is.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct word: *Don't worry — the doctor ____ see you in a few minutes.*
questions.topic: will + infinitive without to
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: After will we use the base form of the verb, with no to and no be between them.

questions.q: Read the sentence and choose what it tells us: *Salem is going to open a small shop next year.*
options: He has already decided to do it.
He decided to do it while we were talking.
He has fixed a date with someone about it.
He opens a shop every year.
questions.topic: going to for decisions made before speaking
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: going to expresses an intention or a decision made before the moment of speaking.

questions.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence: *My cousins coming to stay with us next week.*
options: My cousins are coming to stay with us next week.
My cousins is coming to stay with us next week.
My cousins am coming to stay with us next week.
My cousins be coming to stay with us next week.
questions.topic: the verb be in the present continuous for the future
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: The present continuous needs am/is/are, and the plural My cousins takes are.

questions.q: Compare these two sentences and choose the correct difference: *(1) I'm going to buy a new bicycle. (2) I'm buying a new bicycle on Sunday.*
options: (1) shows an intention, and (2) shows a fixed arrangement.
(1) shows a fixed arrangement, and (2) shows an intention.
Both show a decision made at the moment of speaking.
Both show something that happens every week.
questions.topic: intention (going to) vs fixed arrangement (present continuous)
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: going to states an intention, while the present continuous states something already arranged.

questions.q: Change the sentence so that it shows a fixed arrangement, not just an intention: *We are going to hold the school party next Thursday, and everything is arranged now.*
options: We're holding the school party next Thursday.
We'll hold the school party next Thursday.
We hold the school party next Thursday.
We're going to hold the school party next Thursday.
questions.topic: changing an intention into a fixed arrangement
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: Everything is arranged now, so the present continuous — not going to — shows the fixed arrangement.

questions.q: Read the dialogue and choose the correct form: *A: Have you arranged your trip? B: Yes, I've bought the tickets. I ____ to Cairo on Monday.*
questions.topic: using context clues to choose the present continuous
questions.lesson: Tense review: Talking about the future | التعبير عن المستقبل (will - المضارع المستمر - going to)
questions.why: The tickets are already bought, so the trip is a fixed arrangement and am flying is the right form.

Language review 4 › Comparison of adject.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)

questions.q: When do we use the comparative form of an adjective?
options: When we compare two people or things with each other
When we compare one person or thing with a whole group of three or more
When we describe a person or thing without comparing it with anything
When we say that two people or things are completely equal
questions.topic: Use of the comparative form
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: The comparative (colder) is used for two things, while the superlative (the coldest) compares one thing with a group of three or more.

questions.q: Some adjectives are too long to take -er / -est. Which two words do we use with them instead?
questions.topic: Using more / most with long adjectives
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: Long adjectives do not take -er / -est; they take 'more' for the comparative and 'most' for the superlative.

questions.q: Fill in the blank with the correct form: *This is the ____ (dirty) street in our town.*
questions.topic: Superlative of two-syllable adjectives ending in y
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: A y that comes after a consonant changes to i before -est, so dirty becomes the dirtiest.

questions.q: Choose the correct word to complete the sentence: *The new road is ____ (wide) than the old road.*
questions.topic: Adjectives ending in e take -r / -st
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: An adjective ending in e takes only -r in the comparative, so wide becomes wider, not widder.

questions.q: Which word does NOT follow the doubling rule? *flat / slim / funny / sad*
questions.topic: Doubling the last letter vs y → i
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: Flat, slim and sad double the last letter (flatter, slimmer, sadder), but funny changes y to i: funnier.

questions.q: Why do we change the y to i in *healthier*?
options: Because a consonant comes before the y
Because the adjective has only one syllable
Because the adjective ends in the letter e
Because the last letter of the adjective must be doubled
questions.topic: Reason for the y → i change
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: The lesson states that when a consonant comes before the y, the y changes to i: healthy → healthier.

questions.q: Complete the sentence correctly: *Mona is ____ (young) girl in her class.*
questions.topic: The before the superlative
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: A superlative compares one person with a whole group and takes 'the': Mona is the youngest girl in her class.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *My sister is more taller than me.*
options: My sister is taller than me.
My sister is more tall than me.
My sister is tallest than me.
My sister is the tallest than me.
questions.topic: Avoiding more with -er forms
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: A one-syllable adjective takes -er and never takes 'more' with it, so the correct sentence is 'My sister is taller than me.'

questions.q: Rewrite the sentence using the superlative of 'clever': *No other student in the school is as clever as Salim.*
options: Salim is the cleverest student in the school.
Salim is cleverer than the student in the school.
Salim is the most cleverest student in the school.
Salim is a very clever student in the school.
questions.topic: Rewriting a sentence with the superlative
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: 'No other student is as clever as Salim' means that Salim is the cleverest of all the students in the school.

questions.q: Write the correct form of the adjective in each blank: *The well in our village is ____ (deep) than the one in the next village, and it is the ____ (deep) well in the area.*
questions.topic: One-syllable adjectives: -er and the -est
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: A one-syllable adjective takes -er when two things are compared and the -est when one thing is the highest of a group: deeper … the deepest.

questions.q: Which of these adjectives forms its comparative with **more** and not with **-er**? *happy / easy / difficult / pretty*
questions.topic: Choosing more / the most with long adjectives
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: Adjectives of three syllables or more take more and the most, so we say more difficult.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct comparative: *The test was ____ than the last one.* (easy)
questions.topic: Two-syllable adjectives ending in -y (easy → easier)
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: A two-syllable adjective ending in -y changes y to i and takes -er: easy → easier, like tidier not tidyer.

questions.q: Which line gives the correct comparative and superlative of the irregular adjectives **good** and **bad**?
options: better – the best / worse – the worst
gooder – the goodest / badder – the baddest
more good – the most good / more bad – the most bad
better – the goodest / worse – the baddest
questions.topic: Irregular forms of good and bad
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: Good and bad are irregular and must be memorised: good – better – the best, bad – worse – the worst.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct form: *This hotel is ____ than the one near the airport.* (comfortable)
questions.topic: more + long adjective before than
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: Comfortable has three syllables, so its comparative is more comfortable; -er and more are never combined.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct form: *My brother's bag is ____ than mine.* (big)
questions.topic: Short adjectives: doubling the final consonant (big → bigger)
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: Big is a short adjective and doubles its last letter before -er: big → bigger, so biger is wrong.

questions.q: The adverb **well** takes the same comparative and superlative forms as which adjective?
questions.topic: well takes the same forms as good
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: The lesson notes that the adverb well has the same forms as good: better – the best.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct form: *There is ____ water in this bottle than in that one.* (little)
questions.topic: Irregular comparative of little (less)
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: Little is irregular: little – less – the least, so the comparative before than is less.

questions.q: Rewrite the two facts as one sentence, using a comparative: *Ali is 15 years old. Sami is 13 years old.*
options: Ali is more old than Sami.
Ali is the oldest than Sami.
questions.topic: Joining two facts into one comparative sentence
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: Comparing two people takes the comparative with than: Ali is older than Sami, and the order of the facts must be kept.

questions.q: Rewrite the facts as one sentence with **the most**, ending with "... in the shop": *The blue shirt costs 5,000 riyals. The red shirt costs 6,000 riyals. The white shirt costs 9,000 riyals.*
options: The white shirt is the most expensive shirt in the shop.
The white shirt is more expensive shirt in the shop.
The white shirt is the most expensive than the shop.
The white shirt is most expensive shirt in the shop.
questions.topic: the most + adjective for one item in a group
questions.lesson: Comparison of adjectives - تكوين صفة المقارنة والتفضيل (er / est - more / most)
questions.why: One shirt compared with all the others takes the superlative with the: the most expensive … in the shop.

Language review 5 › Passive forms - تكوي.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل

questions.q: What does the passive voice focus on?
options: The thing or person that receives the action
The person or thing that performs the action
The time when the action happens
The place where the action happens
questions.topic: Focus of the passive voice
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: In the passive we start with the receiver of the action, so the action itself is what we focus on.

questions.q: What is the general form of a passive sentence?
questions.topic: General form of a passive sentence
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: The lesson gives the form: object + be (according to the tense) + past participle + (by + agent if it is important).

questions.q: When do we use the passive voice?
options: When we want to show exactly who did the action
When the doer is unknown or unimportant, or we want to focus on the event itself
Only when the sentence talks about the past
Only when the sentence has no object
questions.topic: When the passive is used
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: The passive is used when we do not know the doer, or the doer is obvious, or we want to focus on the event.

questions.q: Complete with the correct form of the verb in brackets: *The emails were ____ (send) yesterday.*
questions.topic: Past participle after 'be'
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: After the verb be we use the past participle, so the correct form is 'were sent'.

questions.q: What is the difference between these two sentences? *The chef cooked the meal.* / *The meal was cooked.*
options: In the first, the doer is the subject; in the second, the receiver of the action is the subject
In the first, the action is finished; in the second, the action is still happening
In the first, there is no object; in the second, there is no verb
In the first, the doer is unknown; in the second, the doer is the chef
questions.topic: Difference between active and passive structure
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: In the active sentence the doer (the chef) is the subject, but in the passive the thing that receives the action (the meal) becomes the subject.

questions.q: Complete with the correct word: *The novel 'Oliver Twist' was written ____ Charles Dickens.*
questions.topic: 'by' + agent in the passive
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: In the passive, the doer of the action comes after 'by', and only when it is important to mention it.

questions.q: Choose the correct form to complete the sentence: *These cars ____ made in Japan.*
questions.topic: Agreement of 'be' with a plural subject
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: 'These cars' is plural and the sentence is present, so we use are + past participle.

questions.q: Correct the mistake in this sentence: *The cake was eat by the children.*
questions.topic: Irregular past participles (eat → eaten)
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: The passive is be + past participle, so 'was eat' must be corrected to 'was eaten'.

questions.q: Change into the passive: *Somebody broke the classroom window yesterday.*
options: The classroom window was break yesterday.
The classroom window were broken yesterday.
The classroom window is broken yesterday.
The classroom window was broken yesterday.
questions.topic: Changing an active past-simple sentence into the passive
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: The object 'the classroom window' becomes the subject, and the past verb 'broke' becomes was + broken.

questions.q: Change into the passive: *Farmers grow coffee in Yemen.*
questions.topic: Changing an active present-simple sentence into the passive
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: The object 'coffee' becomes the subject, and the present verb 'grow' becomes is + grown.

questions.q: Which form of the main verb is used in a passive sentence?
questions.topic: Form of the main verb in the passive
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: In the passive the main verb is always changed to the past participle: treat → treated, see → seen, eat → eaten.

questions.q: In a passive sentence, when do we keep the agent after by?
options: When it gives important information about the doer
When it is a pronoun such as we, they or people
When the verb of the sentence is in the present perfect
When the object of the active sentence is plural
questions.topic: Keeping or dropping the agent after by
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: The agent is deleted when it is a pronoun (we, they, people, someone) and kept after by only when it is important.

questions.q: Complete the sentence with the correct form of be: *The old houses ____ pulled down last year.*
questions.topic: Agreement of be with the new subject
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: The new subject houses is plural and the sentence is in the past, so the passive needs were + pulled down.

questions.q: Complete the passive sentence: *The teacher praised him.* → *____ was praised by the teacher.*
questions.topic: Changing object pronouns in the passive
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: The object pronoun him becomes the subject of the passive sentence, so it changes to he.

questions.q: Complete the passive sentence: *The chef cooks the meals every morning.* → *The meals ____ cooked every morning.*
questions.topic: Choosing be from the tense of the active sentence
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: The active verb cooks is present simple and meals is plural, so the passive needs are + the past participle.

questions.q: Reorder the words to make a correct passive sentence: *the window / was / broken / by Ali*
options: The window was broken by Ali.
The window was by Ali broken.
The window broken was by Ali.
Ali was broken the window by.
questions.topic: Word order in the passive sentence
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: The object the window comes first, then was broken, and the agent follows in a by-phrase at the end.

questions.q: Correct the mistake: *The school built in 1990.*
questions.topic: The missing be in the passive
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: A passive sentence must have a form of be before the past participle, so we say was built.

questions.q: Reorder the words to make a correct passive sentence: *in Yemen / is / grown / coffee / every year*
options: Coffee is grown in Yemen every year.
Coffee is in Yemen grown every year.
In Yemen coffee is every year grown.
Coffee grown is in Yemen every year.
questions.topic: Keeping place and time at the end of the passive
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
questions.why: After the passive verb we finish the sentence with the place and the time: in Yemen every year.

questions.q: Change into the passive: *The workers must repair the bridge before winter.*
options: The bridge must be repaired before winter.
The bridge must repaired before winter.
The bridge must is repaired before winter.
The bridge must been repaired before winter.
questions.topic: Passive with a modal verb: must be + past participle
questions.lesson: Passive forms - تكوين المبني للمجهول وخطوات التحويل
